engine_findings: TPOT's default Dask cluster binds a dashboard on every interface; an in-process LocalCluster with HTTP routes removed is supplied instead.
TPOT evaluated_individuals stores negated RMSE; failed pipelines carry Eval Error == 'INVALID'.
H2O AutoML cannot be refit from leader.params (unexpected keyword argument 'lambda'); no refit is performed and the result says so.
H2O models that fail never reach the leaderboard; failures are counted from the AutoML event log.
auto-sklearn 0.15.0 cv_results_['mean_test_score'] is positive RMSE, so argmax would pick the worst configuration.

auto-sklearn selects its dummy mean predictor when no configuration beats it; leaderboard(detailed=True) then raises KeyError 'data_preprocessors'. The selection is read from get_models_with_weights() and reported as dummy_mean.

auto-sklearn 0.15.0 AutoML._get_logger sleeps while holding the multiprocessing.Value lock that start_log_server needs to publish its port (automl.py lines 392-397 against util/logging_.py lines 315-316). The lock is not fair, so the server can starve: three hosted Linux jobs stalled until the 180 s budget, all with the main thread at automl.py line 395 and the server process blocked in futex. The worker publishes the port without the lock.

On Windows a thread blocked in a synchronous read on a pipe stalls every child process that inherits the handle (C runtime start-up queries the handle type). The first Windows run therefore hung every engine until its budget; the parent watch now waits on the parent's process handle and standard input is the null device.

A virtual-environment python.exe on Windows is a launcher that starts the real interpreter as a child; a job object assigned after process creation can miss that child, so the worker is created suspended, assigned and then resumed.
